item.title: Harvest Festival — Sat Oct 3, 10:00 AM — Sonoma Garden Park
item.description:
Sonoma Ecology Center’s annual Harvest Festival is a joyful, family-friendly gathering that brings our community together in one of Sonoma’s most beloved green spaces. The Harvest Festival is held at Sonoma Garden Park, a community garden and public oasis just a few minutes from downtown Sonoma, stewarded by Sonoma Ecology Center. The festival features a full day of local music, hands-on workshops, kid-friendly activities and farm games, delicious local food and beverages, a pickle-making competition, and immersive nature experiences for all ages.
Source: North Bay Bohemian, Press Democrat

item.title: Culinary Garden Cooking Classes at Quivira Vineyards — Sun Oct 4, 12:00 AM — Quivira Vineyards and Winery
item.description:
Join an immersive, hands-on culinary series at Quivira Vineyards, offered June 7-November 15 from 11 AM - 2 PM. Led by Estate Chef Julia, guests begin in the organic estate garden harvesting seasonal ingredients before moving to the open-air kitchen to prepare a garden-inspired, multi-course meal. This interactive experience highlights the connection between garden, vineyard, and kitchen, while teaching practical culinary techniques. The evening concludes with a shared meal paired with Quivira wines in a beautiful estate setting. Each date features a different focus, including handmade pasta, masa and tacos, stuffed pasta, global dumplings, and seasonal pie baking. Space is limited for these unique seasonal classes.
Source: North Bay Bohemian

item.title: Fall Wreath-Making — Sun Oct 4, 12:00 PM — Art Escape Sonoma
item.description:
Embrace the beauty of autumn and join us for a Fall Wreath-Making workshop that will leave your front door adorned with seasonal splendor! In this class you will learn how to create a lush and fragrant holiday wreath using a wire frame and foliage, branches, and other dried materials. Whether you're a novice or a seasoned crafter, this workshop offers a warm and welcoming environment for all skill levels.
Silvia Bagnacani is a professional artist, educator, and floral designer with a passion for celebrating the beauty of seasonal blooms. Known around Sonoma for her inspiring floral arranging and wreath-making workshops, Silvia thoughtfully sources local flowers and foliage to create stunning, nature-inspired designs.
Source: North Bay Bohemian, Press Democrat

item.title: Festival Calentano — Sun Oct 4, 3:00 PM — Luther Burbank Center for the Arts
item.description:
Festival Calentano will be an unforgettable night of dancing in the LBC Pavillion. Dance to the sounds of Tierra Caliente and regional Mexican music with Humberto Plancarte’s Tierra Cali, a group from Michoacán known for its romantic style and signature Tierra Caliente sound. The celebration will also feature the high-energy sound of Alameños de la Sierra DMC, the musical tradition of Los Canarios de Michoacán, and the unmistakable technobanda rhythms of Banda Maguey. Festival Calentano será una gran noche de baile dedicada a los sonidos de Tierra Caliente y la música regional mexicana. Encabezando el festival estará Humberto Plancarte’s Tierra Cali, agrupación originaria de Michoacán reconocida por su estilo romántico y su característico sonido calentano. La celebración también contará con la energía de Alameños de la Sierra DMC, la tradición musical de Los Canarios de Michoacán y el inconfundible ritmo technobanda de Banda Maguey.
Source: North Bay Bohemian

item.title: Community in Bloom: Botanical Drawing Activity — Thu Oct 8, 6:30 PM — Laguna de Santa Rosa Foundation
item.description:
Join the Laguna de Santa Rosa Foundation, CNPS-Milo Baker Chapter, and Sonoma County Ag \+ Open Space for a relaxing evening of drawing and exploring nature through art. In this hands-on workshop, participants will carefully observe a selected plant and learn how to render it using colored pencils. With a guided, step-by-step approach, even beginners will feel comfortable and successful as they create their own botanical drawing to take home.
After completing the initial drawing, participants will have time to add color and detail using colored pencils. Finished artwork can be framed, displayed, or even turned into a blank card for gifting. Most importantly, the session offers an opportunity to slow down, learn something new, and enjoy the creative process together.
Careful attention to nature can be both calming and nurturing. By closely observing plants and translating their beauty onto paper, participants can deepen their connection with the natural world around them.

item.title: Mind the Gap: Coastal Climate Impact on Grape Growing — Thu Oct 8, 6:30 PM — Sonoma Community Center
item.description:
Mind the Gap: Coastal Climate Impact on Grape Growing
The Sonoma Home Winemakers welcome Ronald Fenolio on October 8, to discuss how coastal fog and marine winds shape world-class vineyard climates up and down the Pacific coast. Co-founder and owner of Napa’s historic Veedercrest Vineyards, Fenolio will explore the science of maritime microclimates and show how fog and wind gaps—such as the Petaluma Gap—influence grape character, acidity, and flavor profile. Join us in Room 110 at the Sonoma Community Center, 276 E. Napa St., Sonoma, CA at 6:30 p.m. to learn how these coastal dynamics define grape sourcing, varietal selection, and wine styles. Admission is free and open to the public; attendees must be 21\+ for tasting, and guests are asked to bring their own glass for shared wine tasting.
